Social Inclusion Community Activation Programme (SICAP)

Company, is attending all Municipal District (MD) meetings across the county during November. The

Tipperary LEADER programme  
 
The partnership of Tipperary LCDC, Tipperary County Council, North Tipperary Development 
Company (NTDC) & South Tipperary Development Company (STDC) continues to implement the 
objectives of the Local Development Strategy for the county. 
 
Projects under the September targeted call for enterprises and social enterprises to carry out projects 
which will contribute to developing the county’s green economy and employment will be presented to the 
December LCDC meeting, together with other rolling call progressed projects. Under the Targeted call 
the minimum and maximum grant available is €10,000 and €80,000 respectively.  
  
A LEADER annual plan for 2026 was adopted at the November LCDC meeting with the objective to 
work towards full delivery of the Local Development Strategy (LDS) by Dec 2027 through continued 
engagement, collaboration, and innovation.

Planet Youth Tipperary   
A presentation will be made to the plenary of Tipperary County Council on the results of the Tipperary 
Planet Youth data at the December meeting.  Planet Youth is an Icelandic Prevention Model (IPM) also 
referred to as Planet Youth was adopted by County Tipperary in 2024.  
Active in many countries globally, it is an adaptable system that aims to reduce substance use and improve 
wellbeing among adolescents. The questions in the survey ask about six domains of life (home, school, 
health & wellbeing, leisure, substance use and community) and seeks to determine risk and protective 
factors in each of those domains.

School’s Cohort 
Purpose of the Meeting

the evolving needs of Clonmel schools. The initiative is a direct response to findings from the Clonmel

further training and education as the top priority action.

• 
4 Clonmel Primary School Principals/Deputy Principals 
• 
4 Clonmel Secondary School Principals/Deputy Principals

address substance misuse through education and early intervention. 
Sara Cassidy (Aiséirí), Sgt. Graham Deegan (An Garda Síochána), and Carmel O’ Neill (Substance Misuse 
Service) committed to reverting with training options tailored for schools, based on the feedback and 
needs identified during the session.

accommodated during the lifetime of this plan. The Council continues to support members of 
the traveller community accessing CBL as the primary mechanism for allocation Social Housing 
Supports. The current numbers would indicate we expect to meet the target of 22 units per 
annum.
